headline: Russian drone strike on Ukrainian shopping centre kills 16 and wounds 130 in deliberate double-tap attack
deck: The assault on a central Ukrainian mall, described by the EU as 'terror by design,' marks one of the deadliest single strikes in months and raises urgent questions about Russia’s targeting of civilian infrastructure.
body: Sixteen people were killed and 130 wounded when Russian drones struck a shopping centre in a central Ukrainian city using a 'double-tap' tactic, officials confirmed Thursday. The initial explosions were followed by a second wave aimed at civilians and first responders attempting to evacuate the wounded. Emergency services reported chaos as the second strike compounded the carnage, overwhelming local hospitals with the injured. Ukrainian authorities labeled the attack a war crime, citing its deliberate targeting of a high-footfall civilian site during business hours. The strike occurred in a city that had previously avoided direct hits, intensifying fears that Russian forces are expanding their campaign against non-military targets.

The 'double-tap' method—where the second strike is timed to hit rescuers and survivors—has been documented in previous attacks, including one on a Kyiv apartment complex in March that killed 45. Human rights groups say the tactic is designed to maximize psychological terror and civilian suffering, violating international humanitarian law. In this case, the shopping centre was packed with shoppers and workers when the first drones hit around midday. Survivors described scenes of panic as the second wave of strikes forced people back into the burning rubble. Local media shared footage of ambulances and fire trucks arriving only to be caught in the second attack.

EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell condemned the strike as 'terror by design,' a phrase echoed by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who called for further sanctions against Moscow. 'This is not collateral damage,' Borrell said in a statement. 'This is the deliberate targeting of civilians to break morale.' The EU is expected to fast-track new measures targeting Russian drone manufacturers and logistics networks, though analysts warn such moves may do little to deter battlefield tactics. NATO allies have signaled unity in condemning the attack, but stopped short of pledging additional military support in the short term.

The shopping centre, a modern multi-story complex with food courts and retail stores, had become a rare refuge in the war-torn region, offering electricity, heating, and a semblance of normalcy. Its destruction removes one of the few remaining communal spaces where civilians could gather safely. Ukrainian officials said the mall had been marked as a civilian zone with blue UN symbols, though Russian forces have repeatedly ignored such designations. The attack follows a pattern of strikes on markets, hospitals, and energy infrastructure in recent months, part of a broader strategy to erode Ukraine’s social fabric.

Rescue operations were still underway 24 hours after the strike, with volunteers and soldiers sifting through collapsed concrete and twisted metal. At least 15 bodies remained unrecovered, and doctors warned of a high risk of infection due to the delayed response in some areas. Ukraine’s health minister reported that field hospitals were overwhelmed, with critical shortages of blood supplies and surgical equipment. The wounded included children, according to local officials, who said some had been pulled from the wreckage with severe burns and shrapnel injuries.

Russian military spokesmen have not commented on the attack, continuing a pattern of silence around strikes that result in high civilian casualties. Independent verification of battlefield claims has become increasingly difficult as both sides restrict access to affected areas. The Kremlin has repeatedly denied targeting civilians, instead framing such strikes as 'precision' operations against military logistics. However, satellite imagery and survivor testimonies contradict these assertions, showing no evidence of military assets near the mall at the time of the attack.

The international community’s response has been swift but fragmented. The United Nations Security Council is scheduled to convene an emergency session Friday, though Russia’s veto power renders such gatherings largely symbolic. The International Criminal Court, which has already issued an arrest warrant for Russian President Vladimir Putin, is reviewing the attack as part of its ongoing investigation into war crimes in Ukraine. Human Rights Watch called the strike a potential 'serious violation' of the Geneva Conventions, noting that indiscriminate attacks on civilians are prohibited under international law.

Analysts suggest the strike reflects a broader shift in Russia’s war strategy, as Moscow struggles to make gains on the front lines. By targeting civilian morale and infrastructure, the Kremlin may be attempting to force Ukraine into negotiations on unfavorable terms. The timing—coming just days after Ukraine’s much-anticipated counteroffensive began—raises concerns that Russia is escalating in an effort to preempt further Ukrainian advances. Civilian casualties have surged in recent weeks, with the UN reporting a 50% increase in documented attacks on non-military sites compared to the previous quarter.
